area_summary:
The platform side is mostly settled, and almost all of it is a shared, one-time cost. The GameCube renders into a 640-wide EFB. WW uses NTSC 640x480 (g_ntscZeldaIntDf), and the VI scales it to 660 samples. Dolphin's EFB_WIDTH is 640 and its XFB tops out at 720, so the anamorphic picture is the only native route. Dolphin then stretches the frame. With the hack OFF, ForceWide draws at vi_ar x 4/3 and Custom at vi_ar x W/H / (4/3). Against a 4:3 picture that is exactly F = 4/3, or custom/(4/3), so the mod's factor needs no vi_ar knowledge. The exceptions are CustomStretch and Stretch, which are absolute and do depend on vi_ar (about 1.2535 for WW in Dolphin, not 4/3).

Auto never reads vanilla WW as 16:9. With the mod in native mode at exactly 16:9 the heuristic flips to widescreen, both with the hack off (Auto output becomes 16:9) and with the hack on (the hack's W becomes 1, so it stops widening). For any other factor the heuristic finds nothing, so the app must pin Dolphin's mode with -C and turn the hack off.

Four things break today or block the plan:
- (1) Dolphin's -C system name for GFX.ini is `Graphics`, not `GFX`. `-C GFX.Settings.*` is silently ignored, and ReadGFXAspect parses only the `GFX.` prefix, so it honours arguments Dolphin drops and misses the ones Dolphin uses.
- (2) build.py's post-build `patches` loop and dol_regions_test's `t1File` only work in text section 1. A `.sdata2` data patch would land past the end of the DOL.
- (3) DOLPatches are not part of BlobHash. A patch-time-only change does not move the contract, and the patcher's already-patched check sees only the DOLPatches sites.
- (4) The REL's name tags use one `xs` for both position and glyph width, fed by a sampler that returns 1 whenever the hack is off. In native mode the two scales differ (pos F / width 1 if the global 2D compression catches the tags; pos 1 / width 1/F if it does not), so the REL must read the WWWS block itself.

Cheap: data writes from T2 (g_HIO.mAspectRatio at 0x803B9A08 and other bss HIO fields) at boot in ws_init and on WWAP_OP_WS_SET. ops_frame runs before the Link check, so the title screen is covered, and data writes need no icache work. Go-only changes are also cheap: -C args, the setting, the sampler, and the GUI.

Expensive: every C change means a new BlobHash, every player re-patches, and both start saves are recaptured (bundle #1185 and stage 1 into one change). T2 has 0xBF8 bytes free below 0x80414000, shared with #1185 at about 0x100, so large HUD tables need either compact (addr, value) tables or an ArenaLo bump. Runtime code rewrites would need DCFlushRange + ICInvalidateRange (Dolphin's JIT honours icbi), which nothing in inject/ does yet. The REL can't cover the logo, title or file select (it loads after Link + 300 frames) and is only a home for bulk per-frame logic.

items.assumption: With the hack off, Dolphin never touches the projection. It only picks draw_ar: Auto = vi_ar, or vi_ar x 4/3 if the heuristic says widescreen; ForceWide = vi_ar x 4/3; ForceStandard = vi_ar; Stretch = window w/h; Custom = vi_ar x (W/H)/(4/3); CustomStretch = W/H exactly; Raw = XFB 640/480. For WW, vi_ar = (660 samples / 13.5 MHz = 48.89 us) / 52.656 us over (480/486) x 4/3 ≈ 1.2535, not 1.333.
items.effect_native: F = draw_ar / vi_ar, relative to how the same Dolphin shows vanilla. ForceWide gives exactly 4/3 and Custom gives exactly (W/H)/(4/3), whatever vi_ar is. CustomStretch gives (W/H)/1.2535 and Stretch gives window_ar/1.2535, so a factor computed as aspect/(4/3) is about 6% too small there. Raw gives 1.064 (slight). ForceStandard and Auto (vanilla) give 1. Note that Dolphin's 'Force 16:9' window is ≈1.671:1 (slightly pillarboxed on a 16:9 monitor) unless Crop is on. That is vanilla Dolphin behaviour and doesn't affect F.
items.fix: In Go (mods/widescreen setting.go, or next to launch.GFXAspect): FactorFor(a GFXAspect, renderW, renderH) = ForceWide → 4/3; Custom → (W/H)/(4/3); CustomStretch → (W/H)/viAR; Stretch → (w/h)/viAR; else 1. Clamp to [1,3]. Use viAR = 1.2535 as a named constant, documented from VideoInterface.cpp and settled by the live check. Recommend that the app only ever forces ForceWide or Custom, both of which are exact. Also fix the existing GFXAspect.XScale (wwapi/emu/launch/widescreen.go:131-152) for CustomStretch and Stretch, which uses 4/3 where Dolphin uses vi_ar (the name tags are off by about 6% there today). Separately, ReadGFXAspect's default custom ratio of 16:9 (widescreen.go:44) is not Dolphin's default of 1:1 (GraphicsSettings.cpp:22-25).

The PNG's width/height is draw_ar: expect about 602x480 (1.2535) and about 802x480 (1.671). That settles vi_ar for the CustomStretch/Stretch factor.

So vanilla always reads as 4:3 and Auto stays 4:3 (high confidence). Mode 2 at F = 4/3: 1.7067/1.333 = 1.28 → anamorphic (|Δ| 0.053). At 16:10: 1.152, and at 21:9: 1.707, neither band → Active_NotFound → keeps the previous value. A globally compressed 2D ortho (668·F/545) = 1.226 at 16:9, which is anamorphic by a hair (|Δ| 0.108).
items.effect_native: Hack off + Auto + mode 2 at 16:9: Dolphin switches to 16:9 output within a frame or so and it looks right. It can flip back to 4:3 on frames where 'normal' perspective draws outnumber anamorphic ones three to one, i.e. any perspective pass that builds its own 1.28 aspect instead of using g_HIO. At any non-16:9 factor, Auto never widens, so the world shows squeezed.
items.fix: Don't rely on Auto. The app passes an explicit aspect mode at launch (plat-launch-args). If a user insists on Auto, the Go side computes mode 2 only when the effective mode is ForceWide or Custom (or CustomStretch, or Stretch with a known size). Auto and ForceStandard resolve to mode 0 or 1, never 2. The alternative, `-C Graphics.Settings.SuggestedAspectRatio=1`, disables the heuristic and forces 'game is widescreen' under Auto. It loses to an explicit ForceStandard (Widescreen.cpp:74-82), so it is only a fallback.
items.gecko: Dolphin's own Gecko code (0x803FA998 = 16/9) is detected by the same heuristic for the same reason, which is why that code needs no Dolphin setting under Auto.
items.live_check: Launch with hack off and AspectRatio=0. With mode 2 at 16:9 (wwdev poke-u32 of 0x803B9A08 = 0x3F9D70A4, i.e. 1.28 = 0.96 x 4/3, as a stand-in), check the window snaps to about 16:9. Turn on Dolphin's statistics overlay (avg persp/ortho proj-viewport ratio, g_stats in Widescreen.cpp:117-118): it reads about 1.28 for persp. Then try 1.152 (16:10): the window stays 4:3.

items.what: What happens if the player leaves the Widescreen Hack ON while the mod widens the aspect at the source (mode 2)
items.where: dolphin-src Present.cpp:652-687 (fAspectRatioHackW = source_ar/draw_ar; source_ar is multiplied by 4/3 when IsGameWidescreen()); Widescreen.cpp:94-151 (with the hack on, the heuristic always runs unless SuggestedAspectRatio is set; aspect_mode doesn't override it); VertexShaderManager.cpp:52-54 (W multiplies perspective x only). widescreen-culling.md §2 and §9 inferred this.

items.assumption: The hack assumes a 4:3 game. It widens perspective x by 1/W = draw_ar/source_ar.
items.effect_native: At F = 4/3 (16:9) with ForceWide: the heuristic reads anamorphic → is_game_widescreen → source_ar = vi_ar x 4/3 = draw_ar → W = 1. The hack turns itself off and the result matches hack-off ForceWide, which confirms §9's inference from the code. It can still flip on single frames where the heuristic sees mostly 'normal' perspective (the hack would then widen those frames 4/3 more, causing a squash/pop). At any other F (Custom 21:9, 16:10), the heuristic finds nothing → the hack stays at W = (4/3)/custom AND the mod widens by F. The FOV is widened twice and geometry squashed: broken. Mode 1 (clip only) remains right for hack users.
items.fix: Policy in Go: mode 2 only when Dolphin's effective hack is off (forced by the app's -C, or read with the corrected ReadGFXAspect). If the hack is on, use mode 1 with factor 1/XScale (the culling plan) and leave the 2D as it is today. The app's native launch always passes `-C Graphics.Settings.wideScreenHack=False`.
items.live_check: Mac rig with the fixture's hack=True, AspectRatio=1, and a mode-2 poke of 0x803B9A08 = 1.28 (as above): screenshot. The world proportions must match a hack-off ForceWide run (a round object stays round). Then set Custom 64:27 with factor 1.778: expect the squashed, double-wide picture, which confirms the refusal rule.

A const table in the WS unit, `struct { u32 addr; u32 native; } ws_tab[]` for data words (HIO fields, .sdata2 floats). ws_apply(mode) writes native or the saved vanilla, both at ws_init (covers the logo/title, since static ctors have already run when main01_init fires) and in the WS_SET handler. Data needs no cache maintenance. Code words (if any) go in a second list applied with DCFlushRange + ICInvalidateRange (budget-icache). Behaviour that needs maths (the 2D compression x' = 320 + (x−320)/F) is a hook_branchlink to T2 code reading the WWWS block, which is toggleable for free. (b) only for patches that are identical in every mode. It can't toggle without a re-patch, and a per-aspect patch makes the disc aspect-specific, with nothing that tells Go which aspect a disc carries (not in BlobHash, budget-dolpatch-hash). (c) only for in-game-only per-frame work: it can't cover the logo, title screen or file select (the REL loads with its keeper actor after Link exists and 300 frames), and if its actor is deleted on a stage change the module unloads.

open_questions: Dolphin's vi_ar for WW (viWidth 660) comes out at about 1.2535 from VideoInterface.cpp. Confirm it live with a default-resolution frame dump under ForceStandard (expect about 602x480). It changes F only for CustomStretch and Stretch, and it means the existing GFXAspect.XScale is about 6% off in those modes.

Correction to widescreen-culling.md:390: '-C GFX.Settings.*' is ignored by Dolphin. It must be '-C Graphics.Settings.wideScreenHack=True -C Graphics.Settings.AspectRatio=1', and ReadGFXAspect plus its tests need the same fix before #1185 step 7.5 or any app-forced aspect.

Which shared 2D set-up the 2D/HUD agents compress, and whether it catches the dComIfGd_set2DOpa packets drawn with GI_GRAF_PORT (our name tags and lobby line)? That decides the tags' pos and width scales (F/1 vs 1/(1/F)). Wire both to one WWWS 'reserved' flag bit.

With hack ON + mode 2 at 16:9, does Dolphin's heuristic ever drop to 'normal' for a few frames (perspective passes that build their own 1.28 aspect instead of using g_HIO, e.g. the pause menu's 3D items or a JPA pass)? Each such frame would re-widen by 4/3. Check by watching the statistics overlay's persp ratio while opening menus. The policy (mode 2 only with the hack off) sidesteps it either way.

Is an ArenaLo bump of 0x1000 (0x80416000 → 0x80417000) safe under the 48 MB heap plan if the HUD tables outgrow T2's 0xBF8? Measure ZeldaHeap and archive heap headroom on Outset, Windfall and the sea before choosing it.

Should DOLPatches be folded into BlobHash in extract_blob.py, so a disc differing only in a DOL data patch is refused by the strict contract? It doesn't matter if every mode-dependent value stays in T2.

In the app, who owns the ops Queue for WS_SET before the mod runtime gets a Game (§6.2)? It could be a one-shot submit at Start through the engine's attach, or the session's single writer. A CLI submit during a session could collide.
